title: Sugriva and Vali
hook: two monkey brothers, a sealed cave, and the arrow Hindus still argue about
carry: dharma is subtle; even rama's gets questioned
tomorrow: an army at last. so why does everything stop?

segments.voice: Yesterday: Shabari, the forest woman who waited years and fed Rama bhav: god is hungry for love. Bhav: God is hungry for love.

Two brothers. The older one, Vali, is king of the monkeys, enormously strong. One night a demon challenges him and runs into a cave, and Vali chases him in, telling his younger brother Sugriva to wait at the entrance. Sugriva waits. A whole year. Then blood pours out of the cave, and he's sure his brother is dead. So he rolls a boulder over the entrance, goes home, and, at the kingdom's urging, becomes king. Then Vali walks out. Alive, and victorious. And the first thing he sees is a rock sealing him in and his little brother on his throne.
screen: `VALI CHASES A DEMON INTO A CAVE.` → `SUGRIVA SEALS IT, THINKING HIM DEAD.` → `VALI WALKS OUT ALIVE.`

segments.voice: Vali doesn't believe it was a mistake. He drives Sugriva out and takes his wife as well. Sugriva hides on a mountain with Hanuman and a few friends. There Rama and Lakshmana find him. Two exiles, each wronged. They make a pact over a fire: Rama will help Sugriva win back his kingdom, and Sugriva's monkey army will help find Sita. Sugriva challenges Vali while Rama waits behind the trees. But the brothers look alike, and Sugriva is beaten badly. The second time, Sugriva wears a garland of flowers, and from behind the trees, Rama shoots Vali. Vali falls, furious, with a point. You shot me from hiding, he says. I wasn't even fighting you. Rama answers that Vali took his brother's wife while his brother lived, and that the land is under Bharata's rule, which Rama is bound to uphold. Vali, dying, accepts it, and asks Rama to look after his son Angada. Hindus have argued about this arrow for centuries. Some say Rama upheld dharma and kept his word to an ally. Others say it's the act in his story that doesn't sit right. And the Ramayana itself lets Vali make his case out loud. That's a teaching too. In Valmiki, Rama himself tells Vali that dharma is subtle and hard to know. Right and wrong aren't always on the surface, so Hindus are expected to weigh and ask, even about God's own avatar. Questioning this arrow isn't disloyal. It's what the tradition does. When your family argues about what was right, the story says: argue honestly, and let the other side speak.
screen: `TWO EXILES MAKE A PACT.` · `THE SHOT FROM BEHIND THE TREES.` · `VALI MAKES HIS CASE, OUT LOUD.` · `DHARMA IS SUBTLE.` · then, large: `EVEN RAMA'S DHARMA GETS QUESTIONED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a fight between two people you love, and don't pick a side yet. Do what the Ramayana does for Vali: say the other side's best case out loud, in their words, as fairly as you can. Then say your own. Notice what you understand now that you didn't a minute ago.
Sugriva, the good-necked one: the younger brother who sealed Vali in a cave by mistake, restored by an arrow people still argue about.
Carry this: dharma is subtle, and even Rama's gets questioned. Vali got to make his case, too. Day fifty-five, done.

howItsDone: The killing of Vali is one of the Ramayana episodes Hindu teachers and commentators debate openly; in temple talks, in Ramlila, and in classical commentaries it is taught alongside Vali's objection and Rama's answer, often with the reminder that dharma is subtle.

Vali.meaning: the strong monkey king, Sugriva's older brother

Sugriva.meaning: the monkey prince driven out by his brother Vali

Angada.meaning: Vali's son, a young monkey prince in Rama's army

dharma.meaning: the right order of things; doing what is right, which is often subtle

Hanuman.meaning: Sugriva's loyal friend, devoted to Rama

Bal Vihar.meaning: a Hindu Sunday school for children, often at the mandir
